title: Exploring the Role of Neutral 4-Amino-1,2,4-triazole in the Formation of Hexanuclear f-Element Hydrolysis Products

synthesis.procedure: H2O (503 mg, 27.944 mmol) was weighed directly in a tared 2-dram screw-top vial, and NdCl3·6H2O (100 mg, 0.279 mmol, 1 equiv) and 4-amino-1,2,4-triazole (470 mg, 5.590 mmol, 20 equiv) were transferred into the water-containing vial. The loosely capped lavender mixture was heated without stirring on a preheated 85 °C sand bath for 168 h, forming large lavender crystals. After cooling, the mother liquor solidified; the vial was briefly reheated to liquefy the solid so crystals could be removed for SCXRD.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 2-dram screw-top vial on sand bath, no stirring
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Large lavender crystals formed during heating; after cooling the mother liquor solidified and was briefly reheated to recover crystals for SCXRD.

material_class.structural_family: incomplete Ln6O9 hydrolysis cluster with partial μ6-Cl occupancy

synthesis.procedure: EuCl3·6H2O (56 mg, 0.147 mmol, 1 equiv) and 4-amino-1,2,4-triazole (243 mg, 2.890 mmol, 20 equiv) were transferred into a 2-dram screw-top vial. DI water (500 μL, 27.750 mmol) was added. The capped vial was heated without stirring on a 90 °C sand bath. After ca. 20 min the azole melted and the metal salt became an opaque white powder. After 168 h the clear pink solution contained white precipitate and small pink block crystals of 2, which were removed while warm for SCXRD.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 2-dram screw-top vial on sand bath, no stirring
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Small pink block crystals were removed from the warm reaction with a spatula onto a glass slide for SCXRD.

synthesis.procedure: 1,2,3-Triazole (1.008 g, 14.594 mmol) was weighed into a 4-dram screw-top vial and mixed with 4-amino-1,2,4-triazole (0.697 g, 8.290 mmol). The uncapped mixture was heated with stirring at 150 °C for 15 min to a clear colorless solution, then cooled until it solidified. The solid was reheated to 100 °C and an aliquot of the azole mixture (211 mg) was transferred with a heated (70 °C) pipette into a 2-dram vial on a 100 °C sand bath. CeBr3·xH2O (58 mg, 0.146 mmol) was added incrementally (30 mg then 28 mg) over 1–2 h until the solution became opaque yellow. The bath was turned off for slow cooling. Due to COVID-19 lab closures the reaction stood at room temperature for over a year, after which dark opaque gray single crystals suitable for SCXRD were found. EDX confirmed lead (from Pb(OAc)2-contaminated glassware) with Ce/Br/Pb = 1:2.38:0.28.
